Verified _isAuthBroken (cpanel-routes.js:176) short-circuits on code==='CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE', so the api2/fileop coverage gap from iteration_40 is genuinely closed end-to-end. (2) /domains/remove (cpanel-routes.js:1434): the `if (!succeeded) return res.status(502)` gate is placed BEFORE the Mongo $pull (l.1463) and BEFORE cfService.getZoneByName/cleanupAllHostingRecords (l.1478) — no orphan state possible; alreadyGone regex /does\s*not\s*exist|not\s*found|is\s*not\s*an?\s*(addon|park)|no such/i covers all four required patterns and still runs Mongo+CF cleanup, responding 200 {status:1, reconciled:true}. TEST RESULTS: all 3 target files green — test_cpanel_proxy_html_in_200_auth_broken.js 5/5 (incl. new api2 assertion), test_cpanel_routes_file_ops_whm_fallback.js 9/9 (incl. both new /domains/remove assertions), test_cpanel_proxy_subdomain_addon_whm_fallback.js 6/6. I additionally wrote a NEW probe covering the one branch NO existing test touched (HTML-in-200 on the 4 addon/subdomain funcs → WHM-root fallback, plus the WHM_TOKEN-missing surface): 8/8 pass. REGRESSION: byte-identical to the iteration_40 baseline — retry 4/4, tunnel_routing 4/4, addon_from_bot 94/94 green; test_cpanel_proxy_down 2 pre-existing fails, test_cpanel_health 2 pre-existing fails; jest 6 suites/12 tests failed of 379 (identical counts to iteration_40). minor.issue: STATUS-CODE CONSISTENCY (low): the new `!succeeded` gate returns 502 for ALL hard failures, including the CPANEL_DOWN case (removeAddonDomain → downResponse() when WHM is unreachable). The sibling POST /domains/add explicitly returns 503 + code:'CPANEL_DOWN' for that same condition (cpanel-routes.js:1428). The 502 body does forward `code: result?.code`, and the panel's isTransientError() matches on message text (not status), so the UI still degrades correctly — but consider `return res.status(result?.code === 'CPANEL_DOWN' ? 503 : 502)` for parity with /domains/add.

critical_code_review_comments: HARDENING #1 wiring VERIFIED. _detectLoginPageHtml(body) at cpanel-proxy.js:247 is correctly defensive: `typeof body !== 'string'` early-return means a JSON UAPI response whose *fields* contain HTML (e.g. legitimately editing an .html file via Fileman::get_file_content, where res.data is an object) can NEVER be misclassified as a login page. No false-positive risk on real HTML file content.

The 4 direct-axios funcs (addAddonDomain/removeAddonDomain/createSubdomain/deleteSubdomain) call _api2ViaWhmRoot BEFORE surfacing the failure and correctly handle the null return (WHM_TOKEN/WHM_HOST missing) by surfacing code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE' rather than the pre-fix generic 'Failed to remove addon domain'. I proved both halves with a fresh mocked-axios probe: 8/8 pass.

HARDENING #2 ordering VERIFIED: the 502 return at cpanel-routes.js:1455 precedes the Mongo updateOne($pull) at ~1463 and the CF getZoneByName/removeWorkerRoutes/cleanupAllHostingRecords at ~1478-1486. The orphan-state class of bug @Devils_gods hit is structurally impossible now.

Frontend impact of the new 502 checked (read-only): AuthContext.api() throws on !res.ok with `data.error`, and DomainList.handleRemove catches and setError(err.message) — so the real cPanel reason still reaches the user. The status-code change does NOT silently break the panel.

rca_of_the_issue: Original RCA (unchanged): user-level cPanel HTTP Basic Auth is broken for cpUser auth62f9, so cpsrvd answers either 401/403 ('Access denied') or HTTP 200 carrying the cPanel login-page HTML. Pre-fix, the 200-HTML variant slipped through as 'valid data' (panel editor rendered '<!DOCTYPE html>') and the 403 variant produced a generic 'Operation failed' with no auth tag, so no route ever triggered its WHM-root fallback — hence 'can't delete domain', 'edit shows doctype html', 'cant move files'. Both variants are now normalised to code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE' at the proxy layer across uapi(), api2() and the 4 direct-axios addon/subdomain helpers, and every affected route (files content/save/rename/copy/move/compress + subdomain/addon ops) retries via WHM-root impersonation (WHM_TOKEN + cpanel_jsonapi_user). The residual gap I flagged in iteration_40 (api2 + addon/subdomain HTML-in-200) is now closed and covered by tests. Separately, /domains/remove no longer destroys Mongo/Cloudflare state on a hard cPanel failure, so a failed delete is retryable instead of leaving an untrackable orphan. Underlying platform-level fix (repairing the cPanel user's Basic Auth) is still advisable — the WHM-root fallback is a safety net, not a cure.
